title: Vietnam Needs Verified Facts Before Dog-Trade Reform
excerpt: No verified incident, date, location, or agency record supports claims in this briefing. That evidence gap cannot excuse an unregulated trade or delay abolition by 2030.
body_html:
A briefing cannot document a stolen pet, a poison-bait seizure, a court conviction, or an intercepted shipment without naming its date, location, agency, and source. None of those verifiable details appears here. Families still deserve protection from pet theft, illicit transport, unsafe slaughter, and disease risk—but public anger must rest on facts, not invented scenes.

Myths need records, not repetition

Claims about “tradition,” “farm-raised dogs,” or stolen companions require proof. A credible account needs police records, court judgments, veterinary quarantine notices, or named reporting with traceable details. Without those records, no honest writer can claim that every animal in the trade is stolen or that no dog farms exist. That uncertainty does not make the trade safe. It exposes an enforcement and transparency gap.

Biosecurity cannot rely on assumption

Rabies spreads when infected saliva enters through bites, scratches, broken skin, or mucous membranes. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. After possible exposure, wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical assessment. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. World Health Organization guidance does not establish properly cooked meat as a rabies transmission route.

Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains are separate dimensions of biosecurity. One cannot prove the other. Both demand accurate reporting, veterinary controls, lawful transport, and accountable enforcement.

Vietnamese communities deserve accountable reform

Vietnamese families, pet owners, veterinarians, and local leaders can demand records strong enough to protect people and animals. The state’s public-health targets are not the same as SDE’s campaign demand: complete abolition of the dog-meat trade by 2030.

Sign the national petition. Add your name to a public demand for abolition, transparent enforcement, and reforms decision-makers can be held to.
